channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: US midterm elections: North Carolina farmers hit hard by inflation
item.description: On the eve of the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump's unpopularity is impacting Republicans across the board. Many states with seats once considered Republican strongholds are now on shaky ground. One of them is North Carolina, a rural state where one in five jobs is tied to agriculture.

item.title: Michigan Democrat's endorsement of Republican ruffles critical Senate race
item.description: A prominent Michigan Democrat endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday, giving President Donald Trump's Republicans an unexpected boost in a critical US Senate race two days before midterm elections that will decide control of Congress.

item.title: 'No political solution' to anger in France, expert says amid ongoing protests
item.description: With the vast majority of French high schools reopening despite calls for new blockades, and the number of people attending weekend demonstrations down for the third week in a row, are the protests in France beginning to die out? We spoke to one political expert who says he believes they will, saying it is difficult to see who people are protesting against, given that the government has no majority in parliament.

item.title: WATCH: A look at the state of the midterm races
item.description: ABC News' Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott breaks down the state of play as a new New York Times/Siena poll shows Democrats are gaining ground, slightly pulling ahead in key Senate races.

item.title: Senior police officer to go on trial over sexual assault claim
item.description: A senior police officer accused of sexual assault will stand trial.

item.title: Rare ant colony stolen from nature reserve in Devon
item.description: Conservationists have said the theft of a rare ant colony from a nature reserve in Devon is a "significant loss" which "sets back years" of hard work by staff and volunteers.

item.title: How Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion
item.description: A tearful Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 ​days old on Sunday when he finished third for Mercedes in a red-flagged and restarted Mexico City Grand Prix won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

item.title: NYPD seeks info as jogger stabbed in Brooklyn remains in critical condition
item.description: The NYPD said the woman had "sustained multiple stab wounds to the neck."

item.title: US Midterms: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens defects from party
item.description: Democrats sought on Monday, November 2, to contain a rift in Michigan's US Senate race after one of their own crossed party lines to endorse the Republican candidate, as both parties made final pitches before midterm elections that will decide control of Congress. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

item.title: 'More patients and fewer doctors': The struggle for maternity care in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghanistan has one of the highest maternal mortality rates in the world. Experts say on average, a woman dies every two hours from complications during childbirth. The problem has become more accute since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, with access to healthcare for Afghan women becoming increasingly difficult. FRANCE 24's team reports from on the ground.

item.title: Bulgaria's Iotova wins presidential runoff vote amid Black Sea security fears
item.description: Bulgaria's President Iliana Iotova, who favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, won a presidential runoff vote on Sunday. The race for the largely ceremonial post came against a backdrop of a series of drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea that have raised security concerns.

item.title: Two economists studied California's billionaire tax. They reached wildly different conclusions
item.description: What happens in California could shape how America taxes the superrich. But will its billionaire tax fill state coffers — or drain them? (Image credit: PATRICK T. FALLON/AFP via Getty Images)

item.title: 'Consolidation of power': Bulgaria elects Iliana Iotova as first woman president
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 2: Bulgarian papers discuss the country's new president. In Belarus, some political prisoners are held in psychiatric wards instead of prisons. Also: Hitler's Eagle's Nest burned down. Will it be rebuilt and should it? Finally, the queen of Halloween, Heidi Klum, flaunts her most disgusting costume yet.

item.title: Emotional reunions as residents flee Ukraine’s Oleshky during truce
item.description: A temporary ceasefire across Ukraine's Kherson region allowed people to flee the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky over the weekend. They arrived in the Chernihiv region Saturday after traveling through Russia and Belarus, with some reuniting with freidns and family they had not seen in years.

item.title: Dallas Halloween shootings leave 4 dead, 15 injured, police say
item.description: The three shootings in Deep Ellum appeared to be unrelated, police said.

item.title: Football: China refuses to air Real Madrid game after Mbappé comment
item.description: Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast a Real Madrid La Liga match on Sunday after star forward Kylian Mbappé caused a furore in China with remarks he made about former leader Mao Zedong. FRANCE 24's correspondent Jan Camenzind Broomby reports.

item.title: Democratic Rep. Stevens endorses GOP candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan US Senate race
item.description: Stevens and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed have feuded publicly recently over a campaign ad Stevens said was anti-Semitic.

item.title: French school protests resume on smaller scale after holiday break
item.description: French students back from autumn holidays blocked some high schools on Monday, determined to revive last month's protest movement despite a handful of concessions from the government during the break. Blockades took place in several cities across France, including Paris, Marseille and Rennes.

item.title: 'Give them the hammer': Trump threatens Iran ahead of midterms
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday reiterated his threat to resume strikes against Iran, telling a campaign rally that he may have to give Tehran "the hammer" at some unspecified time. Trump had previously said he would not strike Iran again before the upcoming US midterm elections.

item.title: 'A shift in the air': Can young voters turn Texas blue?
item.description: Texas has long been a Republican stronghold. But could that be starting to change? On the eve of themidterm elections, some younger voters are expressing growing frustration with the political establishment. In Austin, the state capital, our special correspondent Tarek Kai spoke to young voters to hear about their expectations and concerns, and to find out whether they think Texas could turn blue.

item.title: Hackers target refrigerators in new cyber attacks
item.description: Cyber hackers have targeted fridges and freezers in supermarkets in several European countries including Ireland – causing temperatures to increase and food to spoil.

item.title: Ministers to hold urgent talks with Poundland chiefs
item.description: The government is to hold an urgent meeting with Poundland bosses amid growing recriminations over the discount retailer's ownership.

item.title: US midterms: Could Senate candidate James Talarico turn Texas blue?
item.description: In Texas, a Democrat hopes to achieve a feat not seen in the state for 38 years: winning a seat in the US Senate. James Talarico, a young elected official who openly and proudly professes his Christian faith, is facing off against Ken Paxton, a controversial figure in the Republican Party. And his campaign is even winning over some of Donald Trump’s voters.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia both hit by cyberattacks on emergency apps
item.description: Authorities in both Ukraine and Russia said that their emergency alert mobile applications were targeted by cyberattacks late Sunday. Residents in Ukraine received messages that there was a high nuclear radiation danger in the capital Kyiv, while Russian officials said hackers had sent fake emergency alerts after gaining access to the mobile app for Russia’s Emergency Ministry.

item.title: Binance users withdraw $3.4 billion after record crypto heist
item.description: Customers of cryptocurrency trading platform Binance withdrew some $3.4 billion of their funds on Sunday after Binance reopened trading. The company had suspended all operations after a cyberattack that compromised over $6 billion in digital assets. Also in this edition: the Wall Street Journal reports on a new US plan to restore Russian gas sales to Europe, and we look at Argentina's efforts to capitalise on Patagonia's wide open spaces to attract data centre investment.

item.title: Midterms: Will Trump backlash lead to Democratic landslide?
item.description: A day before the US midterms, France 24's Oliver Farry takes a look at some of the key races to watch as the Democrats seek to capitalise on Donald Trump's unpopularity. But, says Farry, polls suggest hopes of a Democratic landslide may be wide of the mark.

item.title: 'Manipulated in our darkest hour': Family of Henry Nowak say police failed them
item.description: The family of murdered student Henry Nowak say they have been "failed multiple times" by the police response to the 18-year-old's death.

item.title: With students scarce, college admissions offices get friendlier, less intimidating
item.description: Colleges are trying to transform an admissions process that has often been daunting, secretive and stressful into an experience that's open, easier — and downright friendly. (Image credit: Oliver Parini)

item.title: How does this fluoride-free toothpaste compare when it comes to oral health?
item.description: Many people are swapping out their fluoride dental products for ones made with a mineral called hydroxyapatite. What do dentists say about it? (Image credit: mihailomilovanovic)

item.title: What Vance's midterm push reveals about his potential 2028 bid
item.description: Vance's delivery is different from the president's but his speeches contain plenty of MAGA DNA. (Image credit: ALEX WROBLEWSKI)

item.title: France: Some schools blocked as limited youth protests resume after holidays
item.description: French students returning from autumn holidays blocked some high schools on Monday, November 2, determined to reinvigorate a protest movement despite government concessions during the break. FRANCE 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from the ground.

item.title: Israeli army withdraws from Hebron after operation displaces thousands of Palestinians
item.description: Israeli forces withdrew from a neighbourhood in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron on Monday, ending a military operation launched after two Israeli soldiers were killed in late October. Thousands of Palestinians displaced during the raid have begun returning to homes, many of which were damaged or ransacked.

item.title: In California, illegal border crossings plummet under Trump administration
item.description: It was one of US President Donald Trump's major campaign promises in 2024: putting an end to illegal crossings along the southern US border. Today, official data shows that promise has been kept: arrests for illegal crossings have plummeted by more than 93 percent since the peak of arrests under then-US President Joe Biden.

item.title: RSF publishes list of press freedom 'predators': 'Dictators want to silence journalists'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Thibaut Bruttin, Director General and Secretary-General of Reporters Without Borders (RSF), who says, “When a journalist is killed, it is everyone's right to know what is being endangered.” His warning captures the central democratic dilemma explored in this interview marking the United Nations' International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists. As journalists confront lethal violence, imprisonment, political intimidation and increasingly hostile working environments, the struggle for press freedom has become inseparable from a more fundamental question: who controls the public's access to truth? For RSF, press freedom is not simply a journalist's right to speak, but society's right to know.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump to deliver remarks, join tele-rallies on Monday
item.description: President Donald Trump is scheduled to appear at the Reflecting Pool on Monday.

item.title: Michigan Democrat stuns party to back Republican candidate in critical Senate race
item.description: A high-profile Democratic defection shook Michigan's Senate race on the eve of US midterm elections as Representative Haley Stevens threw her support behind Republican Mike Rogers rather than backing the Democratic candidate, Abdul Al-Sayed, who beat her in the primary race. The move exposed divisions within the party as control of Congress hangs in the balance.

item.title: Taliban voices 'serious concern' over US plan to deport Afghan migrants via Pakistan
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban government expressed concern on Monday over reported US plans to deport more than 150 Afghans from the US to Pakistan for an eventual return home, with advocacy groups warning the removal could endanger their lives.

item.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
item.description: The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front. (Image credit: Bernat Armangue)

item.title: WATCH: Thrilling finishes at NYC marathon
item.description: Sweden's Andreas Almgren won his first men's NYC marathon, and Kenya's Shelia Chepkirui won her second NYC marathon.

item.title: British backpackers in Australia could face changes to visa rules
item.description: British backpackers in Australia could be forced to spend more time in regional areas under proposed changes to the country's working holiday visa.

item.title: 9 dead as jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida
item.description: U.S. Transportation Secretary Duffy says all nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood. The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. (Image credit: Mark Elias)

item.title: DOJ urges sanctions for database analysis critical of its noncitizen voting claims
item.description: The Justice Department is urging a federal judge to consider whether to hold an immigrant rights group in contempt of court for disclosing the results of its analysis of a dataset of alleged noncitizens registered to vote in California

item.title: Suspected far-right activists from Britain 'with tear gas bombs' detained in France
item.description: Five suspected far-right activists from Britain were detained in northern France last Thursday, according to authorities.

item.title: Former Ireland European 1,500m champion dies at age of 34
item.description: Former European 1,500m champion Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34.

item.title: WATCH: The volunteers helping get the NYC marathon running
item.description: While the spotlight will be on the nearly 60,000 people running the course, they would not be there without the help of thousands of volunteers on the sidelines.

item.title: The King to speak about slavery with 'unflinching honesty'
item.description: The King will speak about slavery with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" in a speech to Commonwealth leaders amid increasing pressure for Britain to offer an apology over its role in the transatlantic slave trade.

item.title: UN demands investigation into death of staff member in Houthi custody
item.description: A Yemeni staff member of the UN Human Rights Office has died in Houthi custody after being arbitrarily held for more ​than two years, the UN human rights chief has said.

item.title: DC, Virginia file suit to block construction on Trump's proposed arch
item.description: Washington D.C. and Virginia are asking a judge to block the president's Triumphal Arch.

item.title: Judge dismisses Trump's Wall Street Journal lawsuit
item.description: A US judge has dismissed President Donald Trump's lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Judge says court will investigate government officials in DC golf course case
item.description: The judge wants to know if lawyers tried to mislead her over Trump's plans.

item.title: WATCH: Exploring the ancient origins of Halloween
item.description: Travel expert Gabe Saglie talks about Ireland's boost in tourism from Halloween-enthusiasts.

item.title: Majority of funds stolen in cryptocurrency hack replenished, Binance says
item.description: Around 90% of stolen cryptocurrency assets following a hack on a major exchange has been replenished, according to Binance.

item.title: Man dies and another injured after attack at centre housing migrants
item.description: The man was found with serious injuries at a centre in Tralee, Co Kerry. Pic: iStock

item.title: Texas Democrats see data centers as a winning issue
item.description: Rural Texas voters have overwhelmingly backed Republicans for decades, but Democrats hope voter opposition to data centers could help unseat the Republican governor.

item.title: WATCH: Suspected sailboat thief killed in Rhode Island police shootout
item.description: Body camera footage shows the dramatic police shootout that left a suspected sailboat thief dead in Newport, Rhode Island. The 40-foot boat was stolen back in August.

item.title: Peltola denies knowing of 'any other candidate' on ballot besides herself, incumbent
item.description: The DOJ is acting to "intensely and swiftly" escalate its probe, the top federal prosecutor in Alaska said.

item.title: These House races could determine which party is in control in the next Congress
item.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are on the ballot when voters head to the polls on Nov. 3.

item.title: DOJ says election officials could face jail time if they fail to preserve records
item.description: The DOJ has warned election officials in multiple states that they could face jail time if they fail to preserve election records in accordance with federal law.

item.title: WATCH: How to keep pets safe on Halloween
item.description: Experts say some candy can contain ingredients that owners may not know are dangerous. Dr. Gary Richter, veterinarian and founder of "Ultimate Pet Nutrition," shares more pet safety tips.

item.title: Ranked choice voting explained as voters in 2 states rank congressional picks
item.description: Ranked choice voting has grown as a voting measure for years, and experts say it presents voters with a better opportunity to reflect their opinions.

item.description: Civil rights groups warn millions of Americans could get sidelined.

item.description: You can see more about the baby loons and other animals on "Inside the Enchanted Waterways" on Disney+.

item.description: Dave Merkel, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity company Expel, talks about the major breach.

item.description: Some passengers sold their home to live on the cruise ship full-time.

item.title: WATCH: Remembering Patrick Stewart in his own words
item.description: As tributes pour in for Sir Patrick Stewart, World News Tonight remembers his interview with Diane Sawyer – sharing how theater became his safe space and his home.

item.description: ABC News' Sam Champion highlights some of the must-visit places featured on National Geographic's annual list of the world's best travel destinations.
